mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in FEDFUNDS above 5% for three consecutive months signals a restrictive monetary policy stance, which raises discount rates and depresses equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 70% of triggered periods.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in GDPC1 of more than 2% indicates a significant weakening in aggregate demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: No statistically significant negative correlation (p > 0.10) between GDPC1 YoY drops >2% and S&P 500 60-day returns.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in UNRATE above 4.5% for two consecutive months signals a tight labor market, which increases wage pressures and inflation, prompting the Fed to raise rates and resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not negative in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent decline in INDPRO for three consecutive months indicates weakening industrial production, which reduces corporate earnings and signals economic slowdown, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO < previous month for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: No significant negative correlation (p > 0.10) between INDPRO 3-month decline and S&P 500 20-day returns.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in HOUST and a fall in RSAFS over one month indicates a shift from savings to consumption, signaling a pro-growth demand shock that boosts corporate earnings and leads to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST > previous month AND RSAFS < previous month in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly positive (p > 0.05) in at least 55% of triggered months.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp one-month drop in FEDFUNDS below 2% during a period of negative GDP growth signals an emergency easing, which supports risk assets and produces positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS drops > 0.75% in one month AND GDPC1 YoY < 0%
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are not significantly positive (p > 0.10) in at least 50% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent fall in PAYEMS for four consecutive months signals sustained job losses, which reduces consumer spending and corporate profits, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS < previous month for 4 consecutive months
failure_condition: No significant negative correlation (p > 0.10) between 4-month PAYEMS decline and S&P 500 60-day returns.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent rise in CPIAUCSL above 4% for six consecutive months signals entrenched inflation, which increases the likelihood of restrictive Fed policy and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.05) in at least 60% of triggered periods.
